events.n: [1] The early provenance is according to Denis Rouart and Daniel Wildenstein, _Edouard Manet: Catalogue raisonné_, 2 vols., Lausanne and Paris, 1975: I:no. 297, repro. The painting was number 488 in the inventory taken of the artist's possessions after his death in 1883. Published as in Liebermann's collection in Ferdinand Laban, "Im Zwanzigsten Jahre nach Manets Tode." _Zeitschrift für bildende Kunst_ (1904): repro. 35.

events.t: 19th Century French Paintings from the Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Kurt Riezler, New York
events.q: 19th Century French Paintings from the Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Kurt Riezler, New York, M.H. de Young Memorial Museum, San Francisco, 1949, no catalogue.

events.n: [2] This painting was among 14 from Liebermann's collection that were sent to the Kunsthaus Zürich in May 1933 and later released to his daughter Käthe Riezler. (See Walther Feilchenfeldt’s letter to Dr. Wartmann of 2 May 1933 published in _Max Liebermann und die französischen Impressionisten_, Düsseldorf, 1997: 239; "In the list of pictures that Max Liebermann is leaving in Zurich for safe keeping is “6. [Manet,] George Moore.”) The Riezlers left Europe for New York in 1938. The painting was lent by them to a 1948 exhibition at Wildenstein, New York, and again to an exhibition of their collection in San Francisco in 1949. See Karl-Heinz Janda and Annegret Janda, "Max Liebermann als Kunstsammler" in _Forschungen und Berichte_ 15 (1973): 103-149.
events.q: by inheritance to his daughter, Mrs. Kurt Riezler [née Käthe Liebermann, 1885-1952], Berlin and later New York, until at least 1949.
